title: [DECISION] Resolve ADR-0001: billing ingestion approach
description: The billing ingestion approach is undecided. Two options are documented in docs/adr/0001-billing-ingestion-approach.md. Option A (Worker on CDN route) is preferred if feasible; Option C (separate billing endpoint) is the fallback. No billing implementation work should proceed until this is resolved. Requires a sync with the platform/flag management service team to answer the open questions in the ADR.

title: [SYNC] Billing ingestion endpoint contract
description: The proxy needs to flush per-SDK-token usage counts to the flag management service's billing endpoint, but the contract for that endpoint is undefined. Drive the contract definition with the flag management service team: URL/URL template, auth mechanism (presumed: SDK token itself, needs confirmation), payload schema (versioned), back-pressure semantics (slow-down vs drop vs permanent failure), idempotency and retry contract, and downstream consumer (Grail? separate billing store?). Also determine if the endpoint exists today or must be built alongside the proxy. This is blocking for wiring M3 to the real billing endpoint (though M3 can be built against a mock in the meantime).
notes: Decision document created at docs/billing-contract-options.md. Covers two viable approaches (Worker on CDN route vs. separate billing endpoint), tradeoffs, and open questions for the platform team sync. Key open question: can a Worker be deployed in front of the existing CDN config route?
close_reason: Decision document created at docs/billing-contract-options.md. Two approaches documented with open questions for platform team sync. No implementation until team aligns on approach.

title: Replace UPSTREAM_CDN_URL with geo-bound CDN routing derived from SDK key
description:
The proxy currently routes all upstream CDN requests to a single UPSTREAM_CDN_URL, which breaks data sovereignty requirements. Dynatrace uses geo-bound CDN domains (e.g. cdn.us.fm.dynatracelabs.com, cdn.eu.fm.dynatracelabs.com) per region, and the region is encoded in the SDK key itself (format: dt_server_{region}_{token}).

Replace UPSTREAM_CDN_URL with CDN_BASE_DOMAIN (e.g. fm.dynatracelabs.com). On each request, extract the region from the SDK key and derive the full upstream URL as: https://cdn.{region}.{CDN_BASE_DOMAIN}/server/{sdkKey}.json

Changes required:
- internal/config/config.go: remove UpstreamCDNURL, add CDNBaseDomain (env CDN_BASE_DOMAIN, required, validated as non-empty hostname)
- internal/proxy/handler.go: replace upstream *url.URL field with cdnBaseDomain string; rewrite buildTarget to derive geo-bound URL from SDK key; add extractRegion(sdkKey) helper (splits on _ with SplitN limit 4, validates dt_server_{region}_{token} format); update ServeHTTP to call buildTarget before cache lookup and return 400 for unrecognized key format; update serveMiss signature to accept pre-built upstreamURL
- cmd/proxy/main.go: pass cfg.CDNBaseDomain to proxy.New()
- internal/proxy/handler_test.go: update constructor calls and expected upstream URLs; add extractRegion unit tests

cache.Entry.FetchURL stores the derived geo-bound URL, so background refresh (Fetch) requires no changes.
close_reason: Implemented: extractRegion + buildTarget derive geo-bound URL from SDK key. CDN_BASE_DOMAIN replaces UPSTREAM_CDN_URL. Region validated [a-z0-9-] (SSRF guard). 23 tests passing.

title: Integration test harness
description: The proxy acceptance criteria require end-to-end verification that unit tests cannot cover (cache behavior under simulated outages, SSE fan-out invariants, billing flush under SIGTERM). Build an in-process test harness with: a mock upstream CDN server, a mock SSE server emitting refetchEvaluation events and lifecycle events, and a mock billing endpoint. Use the harness to test all acceptance criteria from the technical spec: cache hit/miss, outage behavior (503 for uncached, 200 for cached), startup sequence cases, SSE fan-out (N clients = 1 upstream connection), billing accuracy, shutdown flush.
close_reason: Integration test harness implemented with CDN/SSE/billing mocks, 31 tests passing. Also fixed nil guard on snapshot.Writer.enqueue.

title: Lifecycle event handlers (token rotation, stage/project deletion)
description: Rotated or invalidated SDK keys must stop serving cached config. All lifecycle SSE events (token rotation, release stage deletion, project deletion) are handled the same way: the upstream event must carry the affected SDK key(s). For each affected key: compute SHA-256(key), drop the cache entry, delete the persisted snapshot, close fan-out connections. The 5-minute TTL fallback covers any missed SSE events — worst-case staleness window is 5 minutes, which must be documented in operator-facing materials.

title: Rewrite SSE URL in proxied flagd config JSON
description: The flagd config JSON served by Cloudflare CDN contains an embedded SSE URL pointing to the upstream SSE service (Ably/ingest abstraction). If the proxy returns this URL verbatim, SDKs would connect directly to the upstream for SSE, bypassing the proxy's fan-out and violating the in-network constraint. When serving cached config to SDKs, rewrite the SSE URL to point to the proxy's own SSE endpoint (derived from the proxy's configured base URL + the SSE path). SDKs must use the proxy for both config fetches and SSE subscriptions.

title: SSE fan-out endpoint for SDKs
description: SDKs must receive real-time flag change notifications from the proxy. Expose GET /sse as the proxy's SSE endpoint. Authentication uses the SDK key via the same mechanism as config fetches. Fan-out group is keyed by SHA-256(sdk_key). Re-broadcast upstream refetchEvaluation events verbatim to all connected clients for that key. SDKs configured with proxyUrl use proxyUrl+/sse for SSE — the SSE URL in the flagd config JSON is ignored when proxied. Event format: event: message, data: {type: refetchEvaluation, etag, lastModified} per OFREP ADR-0008.
close_reason: Implemented GET /sse fan-out endpoint with sdk_key query param auth, cache-gate (412), per-client SSE streaming, heartbeat keepalive, SSEClientConnections and SSEEventsDelivered metrics. 9 tests passing.

title: Upstream SSE client (one connection per flag set)
description: N SDK client instances using the same SDK key must produce exactly one upstream SSE connection. The upstream SSE URL is read from the cached flagd config payload — no upstream SSE connection is opened until the config for that key has been cached. Subscribe as a generic SSE client (OFREP ADR-0008 format: refetchEvaluation events). Reconnect with exponential backoff. Only establish/re-establish upstream SSE connections when upstream is reachable; if upstream is unreachable at startup (serving from snapshot), do not attempt SSE until a fresh config can be fetched.
close_reason: Implemented upstream SSE client with one connection per SDK key; all quality gates pass

title: Shutdown flush on SIGTERM
description: When the proxy is scaled down or redeployed, usage counts from the final interval must not be silently lost. On SIGTERM: immediately stop accepting new SDK connections, drain in-flight request counters, attempt one final billing flush. Wait for the flush to succeed or a 10-second grace period to expire (whichever comes first). Log any counts that could not be flushed before exiting. Exit cleanly with code 0.

title: Telemetry retry buffer with bounded overflow
description: Transient billing endpoint outages must not cause silent data loss. Implement a bounded in-memory buffer for failed flush batches. On the next flush cycle, retry buffered batches before the new batch. When the buffer is full, drop the oldest entry, log the drop event, and increment an OTel metric so operators are aware of usage data loss. Configurable buffer size.

title: Batch-and-flush telemetry reporter
description: Usage counts must be reported to the billing endpoint on a regular cadence without blocking SDK request handling. Implement a batch-and-flush reporter that drains per-token counters on a configurable interval (default 60s, min 10s) and sends the batch to the BillingReporter interface. Each batch includes: per-token request counts, time-window start/end timestamps, and proxy instance identity. Authenticate each flush with the SDK token. On endpoint unreachability, pass the batch to the retry buffer.

title: Per-SDK-token request counter
description: Dynatrace bills based on actual SDK usage, not upstream request volume. Cache hits must count. Implement a thread-safe per-SDK-token counter that increments on every incoming SDK HTTP request, regardless of whether it was served from cache or from upstream. Counter is the data source for the telemetry reporter.

title: Define and mock billing endpoint interface
description: M3 telemetry work must not be blocked on the real billing endpoint contract being finalized. Define an internal Go interface (BillingReporter) that encapsulates the billing flush contract. Implement an in-process mock that satisfies the interface and records calls for testing. Document the expected real contract (payload schema, auth, back-pressure) as the interface spec so the real implementation is a drop-in replacement.

title: Startup sequence (4-case logic)
description: The proxy must never silently start with no data source. Implement the startup sequence: (1) upstream reachable — start normally, load snapshots if persistence configured; (2) upstream unreachable + persistence configured + snapshot fresh — load snapshot, serve, retry upstream in background; (3) upstream unreachable + persistence configured + stale snapshot — load snapshot, loud warning + metric, retry; (4) upstream unreachable + persistence not configured or no snapshot — exit non-zero so Kubernetes restarts and surfaces the failure. Wire into the /ready probe.

title: S3-compatible snapshot persistence
description: A proxy restart during an upstream outage must not reset the cache to empty. Implement an S3-compatible persistence backend that writes a snapshot asynchronously after each cache update. Persistence is optional — if not configured, this backend is not initialized and snapshots are skipped entirely. The snapshot envelope: snapshot_version, sdk_key_hash, etag (from upstream CDN ETag header), captured_at, payload (opaque bytes). Snapshots are keyed by sdk_key_hash. Snapshot writes are never on the hot path — a failed write logs a warning and increments an OTel metric but does not fail the SDK request. A 304 on TTL re-fetch does not trigger a snapshot write (nothing changed). Read snapshots on startup to restore cache state.

title: In-memory cache with 5-minute TTL
description: Without a cache, every SDK request causes an upstream CDN round trip, defeating the proxy's purpose. Implement a thread-safe in-memory cache keyed by SHA-256(sdk_key) (truncated to 16 hex chars). Each entry holds the flagd config payload and the ETag from the upstream CDN response. Entries are populated lazily on first request. On 5-minute TTL expiry, re-fetch using If-None-Match with the stored ETag: a 304 resets the TTL with no snapshot write or fan-out; a 200 updates the entry, writes the snapshot, and fans out. SSE events refresh the cache immediately. The proxy treats the payload as opaque bytes.
close_reason: Implemented cache.Cache, cache.Refresher, and integrated into proxy.Handler. Tests cover hit/miss/304/503 paths, TTL staleness, concurrent access, and refresher behavior.

title: OCI container image and CI pipeline
description: The proxy must ship as a single self-contained container image with no sidecars. Build a multi-stage Dockerfile (Go builder stage + distroless runtime stage) that produces a minimal, statically-linked binary. Wire GitHub Actions CI to run build, test, and lint on every push, and push a tagged image to the container registry on release tags.

title: [SYNC] Define snapshot envelope versioning strategy
description: The snapshot format stores the raw flagd config payload plus metadata envelope fields. Before implementing snapshot writes, the team must decide: the version field name (snapshot_version), integer vs semver, and forward-compatibility policy (how older proxy versions read newer snapshots and vice versa). This is a design decision that must be made before the snapshot persistence implementation is built. Schedule a sync with Engineering to resolve.

title: OpenTelemetry metrics foundation
description: Customers need the proxy to plug into their existing observability stacks without custom exporters. Wire the OTel Go SDK with an OTLP exporter and define all metric instruments up front per the alerting plan: request volume by status (cache hit/miss/upstream error/client error), upstream SSE connection state per flag set, cache size per flag set, snapshot age per flag set, billing flush success/failure counts, billing buffer size, billing flush lag, startup path taken, snapshot write success/failure counts.
close_reason: OTel metrics foundation implemented: internal/metrics package with all 9 instruments, OTLP/gRPC provider, wired into main.go with no-op fallback

title: Kubernetes health probes (/health, /ready, /live)
description: The proxy must expose standard Kubernetes probe endpoints so existing cluster probe patterns work without custom logic. /live returns 200 as long as the process is running. /ready returns 200 only once the proxy has a usable data source (in-memory cache populated or snapshot loaded). /health aggregates both. These endpoints are required for any Kubernetes deployment to function correctly.
close_reason: internal/health package with /live, /ready, /health handlers. ReadyFunc closure wired in main.go — returns true immediately today, ready to gate on snapshot load when that work lands. 6 tests passing. lint/test/vet all green.

title: Flagd config passthrough with token passthrough auth
description: Server-side SDKs must be able to route flagd config JSON fetches through the proxy instead of directly to Cloudflare CDN. Proxy incoming GET requests to the upstream CDN URL, forwarding the SDK token from the incoming request as the auth credential. The proxy holds no credentials of its own. Return the upstream response verbatim (for now; SSE URL rewriting is a separate M4 issue).
close_reason: Implemented internal/proxy handler with full path passthrough, SDK key extraction from .json suffix, 503 on upstream 5xx/network error, 4xx passthrough. Wired into main.go. 7 tests passing.

title: HTTP server skeleton with graceful shutdown
description: A production-ready HTTP server is the foundation for all SDK-facing endpoints. Implement the server using stdlib mux (or chi), wire SIGTERM/SIGINT handling with a configurable drain timeout, and load configuration from environment variables (port, upstream CDN URL, log level). This is the skeleton all M1 handlers plug into.
close_reason: HTTP server skeleton implemented: internal/config (env loading), internal/server (Start/Shutdown), main.go wired with signal handling. 8 tests passing.

title: Bootstrap Go project structure
description: The sdk-proxy repo is greenfield and needs a proper Go project scaffold before any implementation work can begin. Set up: Go module (go.mod), /cmd/proxy entrypoint, /internal package layout, Makefile with build/test/lint targets, Dockerfile skeleton (multi-stage with distroless), .gitignore, and a GitHub Actions CI stub (build + test on push). This is a prerequisite for all implementation work.
close_reason: Go module, /cmd/proxy entrypoint, /internal package stubs, Makefile, Dockerfile, .gitignore update, .github/workflows/ci.yml, and .golangci.yml all created. make build and go test pass.

title: Improve empty_persistence startup: allow cold start when store is empty but reachable
description:
When persistence is configured but the snapshot store is empty, the proxy currently exits with code 1 unconditionally. This breaks two legitimate real-world scenarios:

1. First-ever deployment with persistence configured from day one — the store is empty by definition, but upstream CDN is reachable.
2. Disaster recovery — the snapshot store was wiped, but upstream is reachable and the proxy could recover on its own.

In both cases the proxy could start cold, warm its cache from upstream, and begin writing snapshots normally. Instead it hard-exits, requiring operators to either (a) do a two-step deploy (cold first, then enable persistence) or (b) manually pre-populate the store.

The fix should distinguish between:
- Store reachable but empty → start cold with a loud warning (same behavior as CaseColdNoPersistence but with an added metric/log)
- Store unreachable → retain the current fatal exit (misconfiguration or infra failure)

A SNAPSHOT_ALLOW_COLD_START=true escape hatch is one option; another is making the cold-on-empty path the default and only exiting when the store itself is unreachable.

Acceptance criteria:
- A first-time deploy with SNAPSHOT_BACKEND configured and an empty store starts successfully
- The startup path metric records a distinct value (e.g. empty_persistence_cold) so operators can see this happened
- Store-unreachable at startup still exits non-zero
- The snapshot.md docs are updated to reflect the new behavior

title: Docs overhaul: user-facing README, CONTRIBUTING.md, monitoring guide, happy-path/edge-case reference
description:
The current docs mix user-facing and developer concerns, and several component guides are missing or stale.

**Scope:**
1. README.md rewrite — user-facing: value prop, use cases, quick install, SDK config snippet, Docker/K8s examples, links to further docs. Move build/dev instructions to CONTRIBUTING.md.
2. CONTRIBUTING.md (new) — dev environment setup, build/test/lint commands, commit conventions, PR workflow, issue tracker (beads).
3. docs/monitoring.md (new) — OTel metrics reference organized by operator concern (latency, cache health, billing pipeline, SSE connections); happy-path behaviour and edge-case handling aligned with e2e test coverage (cache_test, outage_test, startup_test, shutdown_test, sse_test, billing_test, lifecycle_test).
4. Absorb open doc stubs — sdk-proxy-ruc (snapshot persistence), sdk-proxy-5l1 (startup sequence), sdk-proxy-82h (lifecycle events), sdk-proxy-qhj (K8s health probes) — complete those gaps inline rather than as separate tasks.
5. docs/configuration.md — verify completeness; add SNAPSHOT_* env vars if missing.

**Why:** README is the first thing a new operator sees; it currently reads like internal architecture notes. CONTRIBUTING.md is needed for open-source contribution. The monitoring guide bridges the telemetry implementation and what operators actually watch.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- README leads with value/use-cases and has a working quick-start
- CONTRIBUTING.md covers full dev loop
- docs/monitoring.md maps each e2e scenario to observable metrics/logs
- All SNAPSHOT_* vars documented in configuration.md
- No open doc stub issues remain unresolved
close_reason: Content absorbed into docs overhaul commit 1b4719b: docs/monitoring.md, docs/snapshot.md, docs/shutdown.md, docs/configuration.md, CLAUDE.md

title: Cap sdkKeys/sdkKeyHashes array size in lifecycle event parser
description: The lifecycle event parseKeyHashes function accepts unbounded sdkKeyHashes and sdkKeys arrays from upstream SSE events. A malformed or compromised upstream could send thousands of entries, triggering one SHA-256 hash per sdkKeys entry on the SSE receive goroutine (CPU-amplification DoS vector). Add a combined cap (e.g. refuse events with more than 1000 total entries) in parseKeyHashes and return false with a warning log when exceeded.

title: Update docs/sse.md to document current and planned SSE behavior
description:
docs/sse.md exists but will be stale after sdk-proxy-qi8 and sdk-proxy-jj5 land, and it currently under-documents the two-leg connection model.

Updates needed:
1. Client endpoint section: replace sdk_key query param with stream_id; explain that stream_id is the SHA-256 hash of the SDK key (first 16 hex chars), not the key itself, and why (raw keys must not appear in URLs/logs).
2. Prerequisite message: replace /v1/config/{sdk_key}.json reference with /server/{sdk_key}.json.
3. Add a 'Two-Leg Connection Model' section that clearly explains:
   - Leg 1 (Provider → Proxy): client connects to GET /sse?stream_id=<hash>; stream_id is sourced from the rewritten SSE URL embedded in the flagd config returned by /server/{sdk_key}.json.
   - Leg 2 (Proxy → Upstream): proxy opens exactly one connection per SDK key to the original SSE URL from the flagd config (scheme, path, and query params preserved verbatim); no auth headers added.
   - How the stream_id in the client URL maps to the correct upstream connection internally.
4. No auth header is required or accepted on the client endpoint — the stream_id in the query string is the only identifier needed.

title: SSE URL rewrite: use stream_id (SDK key hash) instead of raw sdk_key
description:
The proxy currently rewrites the upstream SSE URL in the flagd config to <proxy>/sse?sdk_key=<raw_sdk_key>. This exposes the raw SDK key in URLs (which appear in access logs, reverse proxy logs, browser history), violating the project invariant: raw SDK keys must never appear in persistent identifiers.

Change proxySSEURL() in internal/proxy/handler.go to inject a stream_id parameter containing the SDK key hash instead:
  <proxy>/sse?stream_id=<16-char-hex-hash>

This keeps the SSE subsystem routing logic identical (manager is already keyed by sdkKeyHash), just removes the raw key from the URL and uses a name that accurately reflects the value (a stream identifier, not a credential).

Changes required:
1. internal/proxy/handler.go — proxySSEURL() accepts sdkKeyHash instead of raw sdkKey; injects ?stream_id=<hash>; call site passes cache.Key(sdkKey).
2. internal/sse/handler.go — extract stream_id query param instead of sdk_key; value is already a hash so skip validateSDKKeyRegion() and cache.Key() call; add simple hex-string validation.

The proxy → upstream SSE connection (conn.sseURL = original URL from flagd config) is unchanged.

title: Register proxy handler at /server/ instead of catch-all /
description: The proxy handler is registered at mux.Handle("/", proxyHandler), which means every unrecognised path (typos, health checks gone wrong, scanners) silently hits the proxy handler and gets an unexpected 400 back instead of a proper 404.\n\nRegister the handler at /server/ to mirror the upstream CDN path structure (cdn.us.fm.dynatracelabs.com/server/<sdk_key>.json). Add a 404 fallback for / so unknown paths return a proper error. extractSDKKey already takes the final path segment, so no handler logic changes. Update any test fixtures using different path prefixes.

title: Improve background cache refresh log messages
description: The background refresher logs 'cache: TTL reset (304)' and 'cache: entry refreshed (200)', which don't explain what happened upstream or what changed in local cache state. The messages are ambiguous to anyone reading logs without deep knowledge of the code.\n\nUpdate both messages in internal/cache/cache.go to be self-explanatory: describe the upstream response (304 = content unchanged, 200 = new content), the action taken (TTL extended vs cache updated), and the context (background refresh).

title: Add cache hit/miss DEBUG log lines to proxy handler
description: During manual testing, there is no log output at any level when a request is served from cache (hit) or triggers an upstream CDN fetch (miss). This makes it impossible to trace request flow without adding instrumentation externally.\n\nAdd two DEBUG-level log statements in internal/proxy/handler.go at the cache.Get() branch: one for cache hit (before calling serveFromCache) and one for cache miss (before calling serveMiss). Log the sdk_key_hash attribute only — raw SDK key must not appear in logs per existing invariant.

title: Update docs for snapshot persistence (config, telemetry, shutdown, deep-dive)
description:
The snapshot persistence feature (sdk-proxy-i3m) landed but several doc gaps remain:

**1. docs/configuration.md** — missing all SNAPSHOT_* env vars:
  - SNAPSHOT_BACKEND ("" | "s3")
  - SNAPSHOT_S3_ENDPOINT, SNAPSHOT_S3_BUCKET, SNAPSHOT_S3_REGION
  - SNAPSHOT_S3_PREFIX, SNAPSHOT_S3_ACCESS_KEY, SNAPSHOT_S3_SECRET_KEY
  - SNAPSHOT_WRITE_QUEUE_SIZE (default 256)

**2. docs/telemetry.md** — two new metrics not yet listed:
  - proxy.snapshot.load.total (Counter, label: result=success|failure|skipped)
  - proxy.snapshot.write_queue.dropped_total (Counter, no labels)

**3. docs/shutdown.md** — snapshot writer is now part of the shutdown sequence (drain queue before billing flush) but docs/shutdown.md has no mention of it.

**4. docs/snapshot.md (new)** — component deep-dive similar to docs/cache.md. Should cover: Store interface, Envelope format, async Writer design, LoadAll startup flow, FetchURL repair, multi-proxy rolling-deploy behavior (from ADR-0002).

**Why:** CLAUDE.md requires the architecture table and component docs to stay current. Operators need the configuration reference to enable persistence.
close_reason: Content absorbed into docs overhaul commit 1b4719b: docs/monitoring.md, docs/snapshot.md, docs/shutdown.md, docs/configuration.md, CLAUDE.md

title: Redact SnapshotS3SecretKey in Config to prevent credential leakage
description:
The SnapshotS3SecretKey field on internal/config/config.go Config struct is a plain string. If Config is ever serialized wholesale to logs or a debug endpoint (e.g. with %+v or json.Marshal), the AWS secret access key would leak in plaintext.

**What needs to be done:**
Wrap the secret in a redacting type, e.g.:
  type Secret string
  func (s Secret) String() string { return "[REDACTED]" }
  func (s Secret) LogValue() slog.Value { return slog.StringValue("[REDACTED]") }

Or, audit all log/diagnostic call sites to confirm Config is never logged whole — and add a linter rule or test to keep it that way.

Also ensure SnapshotS3AccessKey follows the same treatment if warranted.

**Why this matters:** AWS credentials in logs are a common source of secret sprawl. Low risk today (no debug endpoint exists), but worth closing before one is added.

title: Configure golangci-lint: config, CI pin, and fix issues
description:
## Why
The project has a minimal .golangci.yml (only 4 linters enabled) and CI uses `version: latest` for golangci-lint-action, which is fragile. The linter config needs to be expanded to match project conventions, CI should pin to a specific version, and all lint issues surfaced by the expanded ruleset should be resolved.

## What needs to be done
1. **Expand .golangci.yml** — add a well-curated linter set appropriate for a Go proxy service (e.g. gofmt, goimports, gocritic, noctx, bodyclose, exhaustive, revive). Configure the `issues` section (max-issues, exclude-rules) and `linters-settings` as needed.
2. **Pin golangci-lint version in CI** — change `version: latest` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to a specific version (e.g. v1.64.x) so builds are reproducible.
3. **Fix all lint issues** — run golangci-lint with the new config and resolve every reported violation before merging.

## Acceptance criteria
- `make lint` passes clean with zero issues
- CI lint job uses a pinned version (not `latest`)
- New linter set covers at minimum: error checking, vet, static analysis, formatting, and common Go pitfalls
close_reason: golangci-lint v2 config, CI pinned to v2.12.1, all 98 issues resolved (gofmt, modernize, errcheck, staticcheck, sloglint, revive, noctx, goconst)

title: test(e2e): happy path E2E coverage
description:
Verify the full request and event path works correctly end-to-end when all services are available. Uses the harness from the E2E test harness issue.

Scenarios to cover:
- Cold cache miss: SDK request triggers upstream CDN fetch, response is cached and returned to client
- Cache hit: subsequent SDK request for the same key is served from cache with no upstream call
- ETag/304 negotiation: proxy correctly revalidates with CDN on TTL expiry; client If-None-Match header handled
- SSE end-to-end: SDK client subscribes via GET /sse, upstream mock emits a refetchEvaluation event, subscribed client receives it
- Fan-out invariant: N SDK clients sharing one upstream SSE key → exactly 1 upstream SSE connection opened
- Graceful shutdown: in-flight SDK request completes before server exits

title: test(e2e): error condition E2E coverage
description:
Verify proxy behavior under failure is safe and correct per the design invariants (503 on uncached miss during outage, billing failures must not affect SDK requests, SSE reconnect must be transparent). Uses the harness from the E2E test harness issue.

Scenarios to cover:
- Upstream CDN unavailable on cache miss → proxy returns 503 (not an empty config payload)
- Upstream CDN times out → proxy returns 503
- Cache hit during CDN outage → proxy serves from cache, no upstream call attempted
- SSE upstream disconnects → proxy reconnects without disrupting already-subscribed SDK clients
- Billing endpoint unavailable → SDK config requests are completely unaffected
- Upstream CDN returns 5xx → proxy returns 503
- Upstream CDN returns 4xx (e.g. 403) → proxy passes client error through to SDK

title: test(e2e): build E2E test harness with in-process mock services
description:
The existing tests cover individual components well (67 tests across 6 packages) but nothing exercises the full wire path: SDK client → proxy server → upstream CDN/SSE/billing. Key gaps include main.go component wiring, signal handling, and multi-component interaction. The make test-int target exists but currently has no integration-tagged tests to run.

What needs to be done:
- Create a test/e2e/ package with //go:build integration build tag
- Wire up all components the same way cmd/proxy/main.go does — in-process, not starting a real binary, for speed and debuggability
- Provide mock upstream services using httptest.Server:
  - Mock CDN: serves flagd config JSON, supports If-None-Match/ETag, configurable to return errors or artificial delays
  - Mock SSE upstream: streams refetchEvaluation events, supports controlled disconnect simulation
  - Mock billing endpoint: records flush calls, configurable to return errors
- Harness must not require any external systems — entirely self-contained
- make test-int must run these tests

This is the foundation issue. E2E happy path and error condition tests depend on it.

title: feat(config): migrate configuration to Cobra + Viper
description:
The service has no CLI entry point, no --help, and no layered configuration support. Operators must discover all configuration knobs via source code or documentation. Cobra + Viper is the idiomatic Go stack for POSIX-compliant CLIs with env var + flag + config file precedence.

What needs to be done:
- Add Cobra to wire a root command with --help and --version
- Add Viper for layered config: flags take precedence over env vars over config file over defaults
- All existing env vars (PORT, LOG_LEVEL, CDN_BASE_DOMAIN, SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) remain fully functional — Viper maps them automatically
- Expose POSIX long flags: --port, --log-level, --cdn-base-domain, --shutdown-timeout, --otlp-endpoint
- CDN_BASE_DOMAIN gets a sensible default (the Dynatrace production CDN domain) so the service starts with zero configuration in dev/local environments
- --log-level flag wires into the existing slog handler; this flag is intended to eventually control OTel log verbosity as well

Acceptance criteria:
- sdk-proxy --help documents all flags with defaults
- sdk-proxy --version prints the binary version
- All existing env vars continue to work unchanged
- Service starts with no flags or env vars set (using reasonable defaults)
- golangci-lint passes

Note: the specific default value for CDN_BASE_DOMAIN (the exact Dynatrace production CDN hostname) should be confirmed before writing the PR.

title: Add LimitReader to upstream response body to prevent OOM
description: The serveMiss and Fetch methods in internal/proxy/handler.go use io.ReadAll on the upstream response body without a size bound. A malicious or misconfigured upstream could return a multi-GB payload, exhausting proxy memory. Add io.LimitReader with a configurable max payload size (default e.g. 10 MB); return 502/503 if the limit is hit.

title: Cache eviction for 4xx on background refresh
description: When the background refresher gets a 4xx from upstream (401/403/404), the current behavior is to log the error and keep serving the stale payload. This is safe for now (stale > empty) but the semantics should be decided: 404 likely means the flag set was deleted and should eventually evict; 401/403 may mean key revoked. Design decision needed before implementing eviction. A Delete method on Cache will be required.

title: Configuration reference and Kubernetes deployment example
description: Operators need clear documentation to deploy the proxy correctly. Document all configuration options (environment variables and config file) with names, types, defaults, and valid ranges. Include a minimal Kubernetes Deployment manifest with health probe configuration, resource limits, and a ConfigMap for non-secret configuration. Reference the persistence backend options (S3 vs local file) and the telemetry flush interval tuning guidance.

title: Per-flag-set fan-out isolation
description: A misbehaving flag set (runaway SSE reconnects, huge config payloads, excessive SDK connections) must not degrade serving quality for other flag sets on the same proxy instance. Bound per-flag-set fan-out group size, connection rate, and SSE reconnect rate. Implement resource limits and backpressure so a single flag set cannot exhaust shared proxy resources.

title: Local file snapshot persistence (alternative backend)
description: Operators running air-gapped or single-node deployments without object storage need a persistence option that doesn't require S3. Implement a local file persistence backend using the same snapshot format and internal interface as the S3 backend. Configurable directory path. This lets operators choose the right backend for their deployment without changing application logic.

title: [Dependency] SDK proxyUrl support in server-side providers
description: Server-side provider SDKs must expose a proxyUrl configuration option to route flagd config fetches and SSE subscriptions through the proxy instead of directly to Cloudflare CDN. This work lives in the SDK repos, not here. Tracked as a dependency because without it, customers cannot actually use the proxy in production. SDK changes belong in a separate tech scoping effort per the technical design doc.

title: [SYNC] Confirm which lifecycle SSE events upstream already emits
description: The proxy handles three lifecycle events via SSE: SDK token rotation, release stage deletion, and project deletion. Before M4 lifecycle work begins, we need to confirm with the flag management service team which of these events are already emitted by the upstream system, and what their event type values are in the JSON data payload (per OFREP ADR-0008 format). Non-blocking: the proxy ships with the 5-minute TTL as a fallback for any events not yet available.

title: test: add /health endpoint to e2e harness and smoke-test it
description:
The e2e test harness (test/e2e/harness.go) registers /live and /ready but not /health. The health package unit-tests /health, but a regression in the harness wiring or in health.Handlers.Health would not be caught by make test-int.

**Fix:**
1. Add mux.HandleFunc("/health", probeHandlers.Health) to the harness mux.
2. Add a test (in startup_test.go or helpers_test.go) asserting GET /health returns 200 when the proxy is ready.

**Why:** monitoring.md documents /health as a supported endpoint; e2e coverage should back that claim.

title: test: redact SDK key in billing_test.go error messages
description:
Two test error messages in test/e2e/billing_test.go leak raw SDK key values in CI/test output:

1. Line ~76: t.Errorf uses %q on TestSDKKey directly, printing the literal token.
2. Line ~124: t.Errorf uses %v on telemetry.Sample, which relies implicitly on Sample.String() redaction — fragile if String() changes.

**Fix:** Replace raw key references with cache.Key(TestSDKKey) and use explicit field access (s.KeyHash, s.Count) instead of %v on Sample.

**Why:** Keeps the SDK-key-never-in-logs invariant consistent in test output, and makes the redaction explicit rather than implicit.

title: test: assert SSE ConnCount==0 in lifecycle StageDeleted/ProjectDeleted tests
description:
TestLifecycle_StageDeleted_InvalidatesKey and TestLifecycle_ProjectDeleted_InvalidatesKey assert cache eviction but do not verify that the upstream SSE connection closes (ConnCount drops to 0). The test docstrings and monitoring.md both state that these events close the upstream SSE connection, so the test coverage is incomplete.

**Fix:** Add an eventually assertion checking h.SSE.ConnCount() == 0 at the end of both tests, matching the pattern already used in TestLifecycle_TokenRotated_InvalidatesKey.

**Why:** Ensures the SSE fan-out invariant (N clients → exactly 1 upstream connection) is validated after lifecycle invalidation for all three event types.

title: Add 404 log tracing for unrecognized proxy paths
description:
The catch-all 404 handler at / (added in sdk-proxy-jj5) uses bare http.NotFound with no structured log entry. Per observability requirements, dropped requests should leave a trace.

Options:
- Add a thin slog.Warn wrapper around http.NotFound, then file a follow-up to dedup/throttle (scanners will spam logs)
- Alternatively, instrument via OTel traces instead of log lines so high-volume paths don't flood the log stream

Choose the approach before implementing. The log spam risk is the main constraint.

title: docs: document always-exit-0 on SIGTERM policy
description: run() returns nil from the shutdown case (SIGTERM/SIGINT received), even when srv.Shutdown or the listener returns a non-nil error. This is intentional — on a signal-driven shutdown, errors are logged via slog.Warn and the process always exits 0. Process supervisors and CI pipelines that watch exit codes will not see a failure exit from a shutdown error. This policy should be documented in CLAUDE.md or a SIGTERM handling ADR so future contributors understand it is deliberate and do not inadvertently revert it.

title: feat(config): make billingShutdownGrace configurable
description: billingShutdownGrace is currently hardcoded to 10s in cmd/proxy/main.go. Operators running behind slow billing endpoints or with strict SLAs may need to tune this value. Add BILLING_SHUTDOWN_GRACE env var to internal/config (default 10s, validated > 0 and <= 60s at startup) and thread the value through to run(). The const in main.go can then be removed.

title: refactor(sdkkey): consolidate extractRegion / validateSDKKeyRegion into internal/sdkkey
description: Both internal/proxy/handler.go and internal/sse/handler.go contain a private copy of the same SDK key format validator (dt_server_{region}_{token}). The two copies will drift as the SDK key format evolves. Extract the canonical implementation into a new internal/sdkkey package and update both callers to import it. No behavior change expected.

title: feat(config): make SSE heartbeat interval configurable
description: The SSE keepalive heartbeat interval is currently hardcoded to 15s in cmd/proxy/main.go. Operators behind proxies or load balancers with aggressive idle timeouts may need a shorter interval. Add SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL env var (default 15s) to internal/config, validate it is > 0 and <= 60s at startup, and thread it through to sse.NewHandler.

title: research(config): evaluate OpAMP for dynamic remote configuration
description:
OpAMP (Open Agent Management Protocol) is an OTel ecosystem standard for remotely managing observability agents. Before committing to a purely static configuration model, we should understand whether OpAMP applies to sdk-proxy's use case — particularly for dynamic log level changes and feature toggles without service restarts.

What to investigate:
- What OpAMP provides: remote config push, health reporting, agent self-updates
- Fit evaluation: does sdk-proxy's role (a request proxy, not an OTel collector) match the OpAMP model?
- Go client library options (e.g. open-telemetry/opamp-go)
- Operational complexity: OpAMP requires a supervisor/management server — is that acceptable in our deployment model?

Deliverable: a brief write-up captured in the issue notes recommending adopt, defer, or reject with rationale. No code changes expected from this spike.

title: perf(telemetry): replace slice-shift eviction with ring buffer in BoundedRetryBuffer
description: The current BoundedRetryBuffer.Enqueue uses copy(b.buf, b.buf[1:]) to evict the oldest element when full. This is O(n) per eviction. Under sustained billing endpoint outages, every Enqueue on a full buffer copies the entire slice, causing measurable CPU spikes at large buffer sizes. Replace with a head-index ring buffer so both Enqueue and Drain are O(1). This was deferred from sdk-proxy-1hj during code review (Warning #3) as premature for MVP with default size 1000.

value: Cache stampede on cold start: multiple concurrent requests for the same uncached SDK key will all fan out to upstream. Accepted as known limitation for MVP; needs singleflight fix before high-scale production use.
